fixture: A pricing module with six passing tests. Four planted mutants survive those tests (three >= boundaries never tested at the boundary, plus an unpinned FREE_SHIPPING_MINIMUM constant); three others are caught. One test docstring falsely claims it 'pins down where that minimum sits'.

evals.name: asked-directly
evals.prompt: I just wrote tests for pricing.py. Before I commit, are these tests actually any good?
evals.expected_output: Finds that the tests never touch a boundary and never pin the constant; says so concretely rather than approving them.
assertions: Mutations were actually run: the report names specific edits made to pricing.py and what happened when tests re-ran
Identifies that FREE_SHIPPING_MINIMUM can be changed with no test failing
Identifies at least one >= boundary that no test sits on
Identifies all three >= boundaries as untested at the boundary
States a count of mutations run and/or survived
Leaves the repo with tests passing and no mutation left behind
Flags that test_a_small_order_pays_standard_shipping's docstring claim is false
